text: reading mission: design a supersonic jet for fast medical delivery: carry 2 kg, break Mach 1 for 5 s, under 25 kg, Boom Prize rules

requirements: Total mass including fuel, structure, avionics, and payload must not exceed 25 kg
Aircraft must accelerate from Mach 0.8 to Mach 1.0+ and sustain Mach >= 1.0 for at least 5 consecutive seconds
Payload capacity must be at least 2 kg for medical delivery
Aircraft must be air-breathing only (no rocket boost or stored oxidizer)
Must complete two flights in a single day on reciprocal headings (e.g., north then south)
Each flight must end with a controlled landing (no crash or uncontrolled impact)
After landing, aircraft must be reflyable within the same day without major structural repair or component replacement
Fuel system must support two flights with sufficient reserve for taxi, takeoff, climb, supersonic dash, and landing
Avionics must include autonomous or pilot-guided navigation to hold reciprocal headings within ±10°
Structural design must withstand aerodynamic loads at Mach 1.0+ with safety factor >= 1.5
Engine must produce sufficient thrust to overcome drag at Mach 1.0+ while carrying 2 kg payload
Noise signature must comply with local UAS regulations for operation near populated areas (if applicable)
Payload bay must be accessible for loading/unloading medical cargo without tools
Landing gear must support touchdown on unprepared surfaces (grass, dirt) with max sink rate 3 ft/s
Battery or electrical system must power avionics, controls, and payload monitoring for >= 30 min per flight
open_risks: Payload bay volume and integration not yet sized for 2 kg medical cargo (shape, fragility, temp control unknown)
Air-breathing engine performance at transonic speeds (M0.8–M1.2) untested at sub-25kg scale
Thermal management of engine and avionics during sustained supersonic operation not validated
Control authority and stability at Mach 1.0+ with lightweight airframe uncertain
Fuel consumption estimates for two supersonic dashes per day lack empirical data at this scale
Landing gear durability on rough terrain after high-speed landing not proven
Regulatory approval for supersonic UAS flight over land not yet established in most jurisdictions
